chapters.screen: Lasso Regression. Lasso charges the model for the absolute size of its weights. As the penalty α grows, whole terms are switched off, one by one: the model chooses its own features.
chapters.spoken: Lasso Regression. Lasso charges the model for the absolute size of its weights. As the penalty alpha grows, whole terms are switched off, one by one: the model chooses its own features.

chapters.screen: Each dot is one California district: median income (x) and median house value (y). This lesson is trained on just 30 districts, one from each income band, so over-fitting is easy to see; 4,128 other districts judge it.
chapters.spoken: Each dot is one California district: median income and median house value. This lesson is trained on just 30 districts, one from each income band, so over-fitting is easy to see; 4,128 other districts judge it.

chapters.screen: A tiny penalty (α = 1.0e-4): most of the twelve powers of income are still in use and the curve bends freely.
chapters.spoken: A tiny penalty (alpha equals 10 to the minus 4): most of the twelve powers of income are still in use and the curve bends freely.

chapters.screen: Each frame refits with a stronger penalty. Lasso minimises squared error + α × (sum of |weights|), which pushes weak weights all the way to zero (○ on the right).
chapters.spoken: Each frame refits with a stronger penalty. Lasso minimises squared error plus alpha times (sum of absolute weights), which pushes weak weights all the way to zero (open circles on the right).

chapters.screen: Validation chose α = 1.6e-2: only 4 of 12 terms survive. Train RMSE $60k, validation $84k.
chapters.spoken: Validation chose alpha equals 0.016: only 4 of 12 terms survive. Train root mean squared error 60 thousand dollars, validation 84 thousand dollars.

chapters.screen: The sparse polynomial prices an unseen district using only the terms Lasso kept; the zeroed terms contribute nothing.
chapters.spoken: The sparse polynomial prices an unseen district using only the terms Lasso kept; the zeroed terms contribute nothing.

chapters.screen: Final exam: the trained model prices all 4,128 test districts it has never seen, a batch at a time. The map shows where it misses: blue = worth more than predicted.
chapters.spoken: Final exam: the trained model prices all 4,128 test districts it has never seen, a batch at a time. The map shows where it misses: blue means worth more than predicted.

chapters.screen: Lasso fits the same degree-12 polynomial of both inputs and switches weak terms off; the penalty α, chosen on validation, decides how many. Same algorithm, now given house age as well as income; height is its predicted price.
chapters.spoken: Lasso fits the same degree-12 polynomial of both inputs and switches weak terms off; the penalty alpha, chosen on validation, decides how many. Same algorithm, now given house age as well as income; height is its predicted price.

chapters.screen: Seven more inputs cut the typical error from $85k to $75k.
chapters.spoken: Seven more inputs cut the typical error from 85 thousand dollars to 75 thousand dollars.

chapters.screen: Lasso shrinks weights and selects features at the same time: weak terms get exactly zero. Limitation: with correlated features (x³ and x⁵ move together) Lasso may keep one almost arbitrarily, and α still needs tuning on held-out data.
chapters.spoken: Lasso shrinks weights and selects features at the same time: weak terms get exactly zero. Limitation: with correlated features (x cubed and x to the 5th move together) Lasso may keep one almost arbitrarily, and alpha still needs tuning on held-out data.
